commitResults.messageTitle: Allow editing task and event details while keeping IDs fixed
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need to correct a task or reschedule an event without deleting and recreating it, which would change its ID and lose a task's completion state.

ScheduledItem now keeps id and project final and lets description and date change together through updateDetails. Both new values are validated before either field is assigned, so a failed edit leaves the item unchanged. Task and Event expose package-private edit methods so changes go through ProjectManager.

ProjectManager gains editTask, editEvent and getEvent. getEvent mirrors the existing getTask lookup. Edits do not advance ID counters because no new item is created.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test task and event editing across model, commands and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommandTest runs every valid and invalid input against both commands. Each rejected edit is checked to leave the item unchanged and to accept a corrected command afterwards.

Model tests confirm that the ID, project and task completion state are preserved. Storage and project view tests confirm that edited details are displayed and survive a restart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add defensive checks to creation and editing code
commitResults.messageBody:
Add assertions for internal assumptions that user input cannot
break: new IDs never overwrite existing projects, new tasks and
events are appended to their own project, editing keeps a task's
completion state, and argument parsing returns one value per
required prefix.

Fail fast with Objects.requireNonNull when ParsedCommand or
parseDate receives a null value, so parser bugs surface where they
happen instead of during routing.

Log failed event lookups and edit commands without an ID at FINE
level, recording only IDs and command names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy creation and editing code to follow the coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Move PlaceholderClientLookup to the test sources. The app now uses
ClientManager as its client lookup, so the placeholder and its TODO
were only needed by tests.

Update outdated comments that still described v1.0 development, such
as ProjectManager not saving data and ClientLookup waiting for a
teammate's implementation.

Follow the Java coding standard: use American spelling, including
renaming RECOGNISED_PREFIXES to RECOGNIZED_PREFIXES, wrap lines over
the 110-character soft limit, and start Javadoc tag descriptions with
a capital letter and end them with a period.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show names in confirmations and ID lookup hints in errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Users had to remember which client or project an ID referred to.
Confirmations for project.add, task.add, event.add, task.edit and
event.edit now include the quoted project, task, event and client
names, so users can check that they used the right ID.

Missing-ID errors for clients, projects and events now say which
command lists the valid IDs, for example "Use project.list to see
project IDs." The project hint also appears in project.status and
project.delete, since they share getProject.

Update the user guide examples and test expectations to the new
wording.
